questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Going on exhange and visiting Australia had both been goals of mine. I had also heard great things about going on exchange in general. Further, i wanted a break after my bachelors but did not want to postpone my studies. Lastly, i believe that an exchange stay boost your resumé which was also a motivating factor-

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country and Australia was my highest priority. Monash also had a lot of exchange spots and i wanted to live in either Melbourne or Sydney-

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was an amazing experince! I met some great people and made new friends. The exchange provided me with the break i needed while still furthering my studies and i got to experience living a long way away from Denmark which was a great and rewarding experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Monash provides a lot of information through their e-mail communication

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Monash offers a free airport pickup when arriving in Melbourne.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think Monash did a great job with the orientation and providing all the essential information for exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It is definitely possible to find housing off campus which is also furnished but it requires effort and it is only something i did because we were a group that choose to do it together. Monash also offers some off campus housing guidance. You need to be aware that you need to attend inspections and it helps securing an apartment if you can pay in full up front. We started out by renting an Airbnb and then looking for permanent housing when we got there. 

I think choosing between off campus and on campus accommodation greatly affect which type of exchange stay you get and you jsut need to clarify with yourself what type you want. With Monash the campuses are not in the city (except law) so living on campus is far from the city. I studied at Caulfield becuase it was closer to the city and the transportaion was not bad to get to Caulfield from the city.

We ended up getting a great apartment from "ApartmentLivingMelbourne". Here are some other provideres that i encounted but did not actively engage with. I therefore dont know if they are totally legit 
- Easylivingmelbourne
- Flatmates --> definetely legit and a primarily for people looking for housemates
- Flexi stayz

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is the best way to experience the city of Melbourne and the surrounding suburbs. Also it feels a bit more like living in the city than what i would expect it does when living at campus. The city offers great choices for things to do in your spare time and a lot of other exchange students choose to live here so social gatherings were often in the city-

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you want to live on campus the possibility is there but you have to sign up as soon as the registration opens. The housing market is expensive in Melbourne but overall i think this will always be the case in a big city when you are looking for furnished temporarily accommodation-

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy! The only part i spent a lot of time on was determining what kind of subjects i wanted.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I dont remember it specifially but as far as i remember all the relevant information needed is described in mobility online and on Monash' website-

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a student coordinator for exchange students both at KU but also at Monash. They are both great and asnwers questions promptly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted. However, the Handbook, which has the unit information, is not very detalied. Unit content are described by 4-5 sentences and the examination structure is only displayed as either "within semester assesment" or "examination" but the type of assesment and exam is not provided until the beginning of the semester. For these reasons i ended up changing some units and i also got some units that were not that great or geared towards economic students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep an eye on the emails from Monash and remember that you can change units when you arrive and get your pre approval from KU updated

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: First of all my view is impacted by the fact that i did not find my units very interesting. But it is difficult to get an understanding of what the units are about before hand unforunately. And you cant see the schedule before you are enrolled at Monash-

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was lower than at KU and the teaching and assesment is very different. More essay type assignement and presentations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They have lectures as at KU. However, i also had "workshops" which were more like class teaching but with the professor which was a great style of teaching. They also have online teaching which i cant reccommend. However, they do sometimes record lectures which  is a great aspect.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BFF5370 - Fintech --> About financial technologies primaily crypto. It also had a coding aspect in Python 
ECC5740 - Economics of financial decision making --> Only actual economics course which was about household finance research 
BEX5200 - Climate change and carbon management strategies --> business focused unit on cooporations climate targets and reductions 
MGI5730 - International Trade policy --> about multi- and bilateral trade amongst countries. Also about trade organisations like the WTO

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ECC5740 - Economics of financial decision making is an easy unit that provied insights in economic research surrounding household investment behaviour. The focus is on the identification strategies, implications and being critical about research. The econometric aspects are more less skipped and not important. 

BEX5200 - Climate change and carbon management strategies can be approved as a seminar

questions.answer:
Visa has increased in price to 7200 DKK 

Some notes to the costs above:
It is generally rough estimates since i was not great at tracking expenses a long the way. Overall there were not a lot of unexpected costs but the level of my costs were expected. I did for example not anticipate spending so much on food. This is however due to eating out a lot. 

"other fees" consists of travel and visa fees 

Communications are all subscriptions that i had during my stay (also including fitness) 

Some costs are not accounted for like the flight to Melbourne which was around 8300. 

Personal spending also includes alchold and generally "going out"

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol is more expensive than DK

Eating out at restaurants and takeway is a bit cheaper 

Groceries is around the same 

Fitness can be expensive but join Melbourne city baths!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend any of these but it seems like there was a lot of options

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of sports and social gatherings you can think of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you have an interest for a sport or the like than try and join a club. But be aware that a lot of these are at Clayton

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The west and east cost are great travel destinations for roadtrips! The west coast is well suited for autocamper since it is more rural and if you go definitely stay at remote camp sites without power. The east cost has a lot more citites and a laid back surfer vibe where it is more rural on the west coast. 

Sydney is also great! 

Go on a roadtrip down the great ocean road south of Melbourne! 

Go hiking and explore the nature! aorund Melbourne as well. Also go to AFL games, bars, parks the suburbs. A great way to explore the city is by going out running.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Their society is very much like the western lifestyle.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not encounter any local students. It seems like the vast majority of studnets and people living in Melbourne have come from Asia-

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some people were not that great at english which i had not antipated. And sometimes it did not really "feel" like i was in Australia since the demographic was primarily asian. You have to get out into the suburbs to meet local australians.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very kind, welcoming and easy to talk to. They also live very different lifestyles across the country which was very eue opening to experience

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Have a lot of savings and apply for scholarships. It is an expensive exhange destination. 

- Be open to meet new people and say yes to opportunities and social events

- If you have the time and funds then definitely go travelling around Australia

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you think Australia is warm all-year-round then this is primarily only true for the northern part (from around Brisbane and upwards). The weather in Melbourne is cold in July since it is winter. It can rain a lot but generally be prapared for all weather. some days it might even be a warm day with sunshine

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of great people and making new friends! Also experincing living in another country, the life as a student in another country and traveling Australia.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the greatest challenge was figuring out how much effort i needed to put into my studies in the beginning

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you get the chance to go on exchange in Australia then definetely go! it was one of the greatest decisions of my life

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
